review_kind: Two complete pinned package static source-vetting decisions, not governed semantic verification
macro_findings: Deno parent tree contains a nested independently front-mattered Oak package: 14 distinct source files in the parent tree, 7 parent-owned and 7 Oak-owned; count two first-class SKILL.md identities, not 21 separate reviewed files.
Oak six-reference bundle contradicts its parent v17 API guidance with pre-v13 request body calls, legacy import paths and a development JWT secret fallback; reading only SKILL.md would miss this.
Deno parent reference bundle mixes Deno 2/JSR guidance with obsolete std URLs and Fresh 1 conventions; examples persist and expose user email PII without route authorization.
Neither source permission flags nor presence of auth middleware supplies user authorization to publish, deploy, mutate customer data, expose logs, or enable telemetry.
No admission, governed verification pair, external security scan or behavioral validation; distinct eligible denominator remains unknown.

records.name: deno
records.license: Pinned root MIT LICENSE blob 0e8b6e6d8678128ebfcc28d7cad91fa9ed7f2354; no separate LICENSE in inspected package subtree; external dependencies and linked examples have independent terms
records.specific_capability: Configure Deno 2 runtime permissions, KV-backed APIs and deployment
records.trigger: Deno 2 runtime, JSR/npm, Deno KV, deno.json and Fresh framework
records.nontrigger: Oak-specific deep architecture, Node/Bun projects, frontend-only TypeScript
records.dependencies: Deno 2, JSR std/Hono, Zod, Deno KV, six direct bundled references plus separate nested Oak first-class package (not counted as a second parent-owned reference)
records.authority_and_side_effects: Example Hono GET/POST routes persist and disclose user email records without authentication or per-user access control; deployment and deno publish/compile examples lack separate project/production authority.
records.privacy_and_egress: Email PII in persistent Deno KV and read APIs, OTEL export, Stripe env permissions, deployment secrets; require per-destination and tenant authorization.
records.portability_and_freshness: Deno 2.x current in parent, but bundled deno-essentials/deno-runtime/deployment/Fresh references include obsolete std imports, Fresh 1 API and unverified platform/pricing claims; no execution evidence.
records.rationale: Parent uses unauthenticated GET/list/create user endpoints with email PII persisted to KV; a Fresh reference uses unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML and unauthenticated PUT/DELETE. Bundled deployment includes a literal sample database credential URL and legacy imports. Strong least-privilege/lockfile and runtime decision guidance can be extracted without unchanged reuse.
records.required_authorization_boundary: Explicit authorization for user data access/storage, API writes, production deployment, telemetry, credential provisioning, package publishing and persistent cloud resources.
records.hard_fail_reason: Unscoped PII storage/disclosure and mutations in sample API plus unbounded deployment/publishing guidance and outdated bundled references.

records.name: oak-backend
records.license: Pinned root MIT LICENSE blob 0e8b6e6d8678128ebfcc28d7cad91fa9ed7f2354; no separate LICENSE in inspected package subtree; external dependencies and linked examples have independent terms
records.specific_capability: Design Oak middleware, typed routing and request-isolated testing
records.trigger: Oak on Deno, middleware/router/context and TypeScript API design
records.nontrigger: Generic Deno permissions, Node Express or Hono-only API
records.dependencies: Deno 2, Oak 17 on JSR, Zod, std/assert; six bundled references including legacy Oak imports and pre-v13 body calls
records.authority_and_side_effects: Code examples create project files, modify dependencies, write orders and provide production deployment instructions without a distinct approval boundary for writes, user data, deployment destination or live traffic.
records.privacy_and_egress: Order/customer identifiers, JWT auth, logs, request paths and DB operations; require scoped identity, tenant, data retention and egress authorization.
records.portability_and_freshness: Deno 2/Oak 17 assumed; references mix legacy oak imports and pre-v13 ctx.request.body().value despite parent saying v13+ API. Not executed.
records.rationale: Six bundled references materially contradict the v17 API guidance; setup reference supplies a dev-secret fallback, routing reference performs CRUD without authorization, performance reference uses non-atomic KV rate-limit increments, and deployment reference gives broad permission flags. Preserve Oak router/app.handle testing and dependency injection patterns as reference only.
records.required_authorization_boundary: Explicit user/project authorization for local writes, live API/database mutations, deployment, credentials, private logs and remote destinations; validate per-route access controls.
records.hard_fail_reason: Unbounded live CRUD/deployment guidance plus contradictory legacy API references and unsafe dev-secret fallback.
